observation.visible_scene: A person wearing black trousers and black shoes stands on a grey concrete surface, holding a large orange pneumatic breaker/jackhammer that is fed by a dark air hose with a metal valve fitting dangling to the left. The tool's long steel chisel bit is pressed against a yellow wooden board lying flat on the ground; the board already shows multiple gouged, splintered depressions and a round hole near one corner. A metal strip and a concrete expansion seam are visible in the background.
visible_changes: The breaker is held with the chisel bit in continuous contact with the board, and the tool plus the operator's body show small frame-to-frame jitter consistent with a running, vibrating pneumatic tool.

The bit's contact point is dragged across the board's surface over the excerpt: starting near the upper-central damaged area, moving toward the right edge, and later toward the lower-right portion of the board.

The operator shifts stance during the clip: the left foot moves from a wide position toward the board and the legs partially cross, while the right foot stays roughly planted near the board's upper edge.

The camera slowly tilts/pans upward across the segment: the background seam drifts downward in frame, the yellow board and its round hole slide toward and partly out of the bottom edge, and the operator's hand gripping the tool's upper handle (out of frame early on) becomes visible in the later frames.
The pre-existing gouges and the round hole on the board remain visible throughout; no new hole or large deformation is clearly formed within the excerpt.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the tool is actively firing or merely resting on the board is not directly confirmable from stills.
What caused the existing board damage and whether the work continues to completion after the last frame.
The operator's upper body, head, and the full grip configuration before the camera tilt revealed the top hand.
uncertain_details: The apparent upward reveal of the top hand is likely camera tilt rather than the hand moving, but the two cannot be fully separated from the frames.
Small positional shifts of the bit and board mix tool vibration, the operator repositioning, and handheld camera motion; exact attribution is uncertain.
Whether the board itself translates or only its image position changes due to camera movement is not fully resolved.
